vectors.description: SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with single-element prefix (results in PUBLISH messages for matching tracks)

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with FORWARD parameter set to 0. In draft-21 the publisher must communicate the resulting initial Subscription Parameters explicitly in each PUBLISH; draft-19's special-case FORWARD and GROUP_ORDER echo rules are gone
SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN parameter (USE_VALUE type=0, value='tracks-tok'). Section 9.20.3 forbids copying it into the resulting PUBLISH
SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with zero-element prefix (subscribes to all tracks)
SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES (0x35) set to 0 — the resulting PUBLISH messages should carry an empty Track Properties field

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with TRACK_PROPERTY_FILTER (0x29): SetID 0, Track Property Type 0x0E, value range 1-1 — filters which PUBLISH messages are forwarded. 0x29 is the one range filter that may not appear inside FILL_PARAMETERS
SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS with OBJECTID_FILTER (0x26): SetID 0, Object ID range 0-4, used as an initial subscription filter for the resulting PUBLISH messages

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS carrying TRACK_PROPERTY_FILTER twice: DEFAULT_PUBLISHER_PRIORITY (0x0E) equal to 1 in set 0, and DEFAULT_PUBLISHER_GROUP_ORDER (0x22) between 1 and 2 in set 1. Section 3.3.2 gives this type its own sentence: "The Track Property filter parameter MAY appear multiple times in a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS message or REQUEST_UPDATE for it." The two instances differ in SetID and in Property Type, so neither half of the (Parameter Type, SetID, Property Type) triple the same section forbids repeating is repeated here. Both Property Types are even, which is what makes them integer-valued and a range over them meaningful.

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS carrying a two-field LOCATION_FILTER whose StartGroup and StartObject are both 0, the Next Object, so each resulting subscription joins its Track at the Next Object. Section 9.18.1: "Any Parameter that can be specified on a Subscription (ie: in SUBSCRIBE) is valid in SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, unless otherwise specified." The same section then tells the subscriber it "can specify a Location Filter and optionally include FILL_PARAMETERS" to join the Tracks the resulting PUBLISHes start. The LOCATION_FILTER definition (Section 9.20.10) names FETCH, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, REQUEST_UPDATE and PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY, the FILL_PARAMETERS definition (Section 9.20.16) names SUBSCRIBE and REQUEST_UPDATE, and Section 9.20.1 makes a parameter in any other message a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The two readings disagree from draft-20 on, and only about LOCATION_FILTER and FILL_PARAMETERS: for every other SUBSCRIBE parameter the definition is the "otherwise specified". This corpus admits those two on SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, because Section 9.18.1 instructs the subscriber to send them, and refuses every other parameter the definitions leave out, so this frame decodes rather than closing the session

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS carrying a two-field LOCATION_FILTER whose StartGroup and StartObject are both 0, the Next Object, followed by an empty FILL_PARAMETERS (0x23, Type Delta 0x02 from 0x21), the pair Section 9.18.1 names for joining the Tracks the resulting PUBLISHes start (Section 3.5). The empty FILL_PARAMETERS is Length 1 carrying its Number of Parameters, 00. Both parameters are admitted on SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS for the reason with-location-filter gives; a decoder that admits LOCATION_FILTER here and not FILL_PARAMETERS refuses this frame

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS carrying FILL_PARAMETERS (0x23) alone, its value a two-field LOCATION_FILTER selecting the fill range {100,0} onward for each resulting subscription. The FILL_PARAMETERS definition (Section 9.20.16) names SUBSCRIBE and REQUEST_UPDATE only; Section 9.18.1 names it for SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, and this corpus admits it there for the reason with-location-filter gives. With no LOCATION_FILTER before it, the outer Type Delta is the absolute type 0x23

SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS carrying OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT (0x02), 5000 ms. Its definition (Section 9.20.5): "The OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT parameter (Parameter Type 0x02) is a varint. It MAY appear in a SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, or REQUEST_UPDATE message." Section 9.20.1 requires the receiver to close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a parameter appears in a message its definition does not name. Section 9.18.1's "Any Parameter that can be specified on a Subscription (ie: in SUBSCRIBE) is valid in SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, unless otherwise specified" does not admit it, because the definition is that otherwise-specified. Only LOCATION_FILTER and FILL_PARAMETERS, which Section 9.18.1 names for SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS explicitly, are admitted past their definitions
vectors.error_detail: OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT may appear in SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH or REQUEST_UPDATE; SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS is none of those
